headline: GTA 6 pre-orders confirmed for June 25 sending Take-Two surging +5%, while Pilbara Minerals had a rough day dropping -4.7% as lithium market headwinds persist — and the RBA left rates on hold, giving Aussie borrowers some breathing room.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had its worst session in the portfolio today, dropping nearly 5% to $5.88. The lithium market remains in surplus — there's more lithium supply around the world than buyers need right now — which keeps downward pressure on prices and on miners like PLS. News around the Pilgangoora expansion is also sparking debate about whether adding more supply is the right call in this market.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Last night was a big one for Take-Two. Rockstar Games officially confirmed GTA 6 pre-orders kick off June 25, releasing the game's cover art and with reports that the price tag will be around US$80. That's a massive catalyst — this is one of the most anticipated game launches ever, and pre-orders starting means real money flowing in soon.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google had a solid night last session, up 1.48% to US$367.46. Analyst commentary highlighted that Google Cloud is actually outperforming rivals Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services, and that Alphabet has a staggering $462 billion in contracted backlog — basically future revenue already locked in. The market liked the story.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.74% today to $94.44. Emerging market ETFs tend to drift lower when global risk appetite softens or the broader ASX has a weak session — which it did today, falling 0.92%. No single dramatic catalyst, just a softer day across the board.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased back 0.56% today to $76.83 as the ASX had a down session. This fund holds a broad mix of Aussie and international shares, so it tends to track the overall market mood. Nothing alarming — just a soft day dragging it slightly lower.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.61% today to $8.10. Oil prices are basically flat right now (WTI crude just under US$77), but there's uncertainty around the Iran conflict's impact on global supply and demand — the IEA is expecting both supply and demand to contract in 2026. Energy stocks are in a bit of a holding pattern.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.22% today to $18.16, a small positive in an otherwise mixed session. The AI theme remains intact, and some analysts are pointing to further market gains in the next six months as a tailwind for tech-heavy ETFs like this one.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was barely moved last session, up just 0.13% to US$379.40. No major news catalyst overnight. The stock is still sitting well below your average purchase price, so this is a quiet holding period for now.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up a tiny 0.07% to $525.46 today. The US market had a strong night last session (NASDAQ up nearly 2%), and that's slowly flowing through into ASX-listed US market ETFs. VTS is one of your steadier holdings — sitting slightly ahead of what you paid.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 pre-orders open June 25 — big week for TTWO
watch_today.detail: Rockstar officially confirmed GTA 6 pre-orders start June 25, with cover art revealed and reports pointing to an ~US$80 price point. This is one of the biggest game launches in history and the market reacted — TTWO surged nearly 5% last session. The next catalyst to watch is the pre-order numbers and any Trailer #3 announcement. This week matters.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continuing, watch your levels
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped 4.7% today to $5.88, and you're now down 12.76% on this position. The lithium market has a supply surplus problem — too much lithium, not enough demand — and that's not resolving quickly. The Pilgangoora expansion debate adds more uncertainty. No clear bottom in sight yet.

watch_today.title: GOOG momentum building — Google Cloud story is strong
watch_today.detail: Alphabet rose 1.48% last session and analyst research is making a compelling case: Google Cloud is outperforming Azure and AWS, and the company has a $462 billion contracted backlog. You're up 19.5% on this position. The fundamentals look solid — no reason to sell.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — relief for ASX and mortgage holders
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank left interest rates on hold at its June meeting. This is good news for anyone with a mortgage, and it tends to be a mild positive for the sharemarket since lower-for-longer rates make shares more attractive. No immediate action needed, but it's a supportive backdrop for your ASX holdings.

watch_today.title: ASX had a down day — broad-based softness across your ETFs
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 fell 0.92% today to 8,828 points. Your ASX-listed ETFs (VDHG, VGE, FUEL) all closed slightly lower as a result. This isn't panic territory — just a soft session. The US NASDAQ was up nearly 2% last night, which should provide some support when US markets open tonight.

watch_today.title: MSFT still underwater — watching for a catalyst
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is your biggest loss in dollar terms, sitting $57 AUD below what you paid. The stock is barely moving and there's no major news right now. Earnings are the next real catalyst — worth keeping an eye on the calendar. Hold for now.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Friday, dropping 0.92% to close at 8,828 — broad-based selling across sectors. Meanwhile last night on Wall Street it was a completely different story: the NASDAQ surged 1.91% and the S&P 500 climbed 1.08%, driven by strong tech momentum. Gold pulled back 1.21% to around US$4,173, oil is basically flat near US$76.54, and the Aussie dollar is holding steady at about 70.2 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big domestic stories today: the RBA gave mortgage holders a break by keeping rates on hold, and the Greens are blocking NDIS reforms in the Senate — threatening a key Labor budget item.

stories.title: RBA leaves interest rates on hold — relief for borrowers
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept the cash rate on hold at its June meeting, giving homeowners and businesses a break after a punishing rate-hiking cycle. For everyday Aussies with variable-rate mortgages, it means no change to repayments this month. For investors, a steady rate environment tends to be mildly positive for shares — it signals the RBA doesn't think the economy is overheating enough to need further cooling. Markets had largely expected this outcome.

stories.title: NDIS reforms face delay as Greens play hardball on budget
stories.why_it_matters: The Greens are blocking Labor's proposed NDIS (disability support) reforms in the Senate, using them as leverage in broader budget negotiations. The NDIS budget has been a major spending pressure for the government, and Labor had been counting on reforms to rein in costs. A delay means billions in savings might not materialise on the timeline the government planned, complicating the budget bottom line. This is a political standoff to watch — it could affect other spending priorities too.

ai.summary: The big AI story this week is global governance — the G7 summit saw Trump meet Big Tech leaders as world governments scramble to figure out who makes the rules for AI. Meanwhile the US approach is being contrasted sharply with the EU's more structured rulebook.

stories.title: G7 AI Summit: Trump meets Big Tech as nations fight over who controls AI
stories.why_it_matters: The G7 AI Summit brought together world leaders and the heads of major tech companies — think Google, Microsoft, OpenAI — to hash out how AI should be governed globally. The key tension is between countries wanting to keep AI development fast and unregulated (the US approach) versus those pushing for binding rules (like the EU). For investors in GOOG and MSFT, the outcome of these talks matters: heavy-handed regulation could slow AI product rollouts and hit revenue, while a light-touch regime is a green light for growth.

stories.title: The White House is making up AI rules on the fly
stories.why_it_matters: According to WIRED, the Trump White House has no coherent AI policy framework — it's essentially improvising as it goes, issuing executive orders and guidance without a consistent strategy. This matters because the US is home to most of the world's leading AI companies. Regulatory uncertainty can slow enterprise adoption and create compliance headaches for firms like Google and Microsoft, but in the short term a 'hands off' approach tends to let tech companies move faster.

stories.title: A tale of two AI policy regimes: US vs the world
stories.why_it_matters: Foreign Policy breaks down how the world is splitting into two camps on AI: the US, which is favouring speed and minimal rules, versus the EU, which has its comprehensive AI Act with strict obligations on high-risk AI systems. For companies operating globally (like Alphabet and Microsoft), this creates a compliance patchwork — they may need to build different versions of products for different markets. It's a growing cost of doing business in AI.

sport.summary: Round 16 NRL is underway — the Dolphins made it seven wins in a row, the Knights survived a scare against the Dragons, and the Panthers are leading the Titans 12-6 at half time at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast. AFL news is dominated by the Tony Modra crash recovery update.

stories.title: Dolphins make it seven in a row, bash injury-hit Tigers 36-22
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins romped to a 36-22 win over Wests Tigers at Campbelltown today, making it seven consecutive wins and cementing their top-of-the-table credentials. The Tigers were badly hit by injuries going in, which softened the challenge. 'Mission accomplished' was the Dolphins' camp verdict. They're building serious momentum heading towards finals football.

stories.title: Panthers lead Titans 12-6 at half time at Cbus Super Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Right in your backyard at Cbus Super Stadium — the Titans are trailing the Panthers 12-6 at half time. Penrith are starting hot despite resting some of their State of Origin stars, which tells you something about the depth of their squad. The Titans will need a big second half to keep their season on track.

stories.title: Knights survive massive scare, beat Dragons 22-20
stories.why_it_matters: The Knights held on by the skin of their teeth on Friday night, beating the Dragons 22-20 at McDonald Jones Stadium. The Dragons had a crucial missed shot at goal late in the match that would have tied or won the game, handing Newcastle the two points. A nervy win, but a win is a win for Newcastle.

stories.title: AFL icon Tony Modra stable and recovering after major surgery
stories.why_it_matters: Former Adelaide Crows champion Tony Modra is 'awake with his wife and kids' and described as stable after a harrowing car crash that required major surgery. Reports say everyone close to him was genuinely concerned, so this is a positive update after a very scary situation. Modra is one of the most beloved figures in Crows history, famous for his spectacular marking. Great to hear he's on the mend.
